chapter: Dave and Iola: faith and values
title: Iola's role in Dave's music and the meaning of his religious pieces
summary: Monk recalls Iola's opinions on Dave's work; Chris explains Dave's Biblical-text pieces as pointed critiques of hypocrisy and racism.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I’ve had the privilege of being in the Brubeck house twice to interview your parents. And I was struck, Dave had been working on a piece the day I got there and he took me to the piano and he said come on. It was for piano and voice, and the war in Afghanistan had just started and it was reflective of that. And it was interesting because he said, “Iola said no one will want to sing it. It’s too sad.” And I got this little picture of their back and forth and her opinions, voicing her opinions about his music, in addition to handling so much of the business. And it was just a neat moment. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Yeah well she was deeply involved in the evolution of all the religious pieces he wrote and there’s like 17 or 18 of them where a lot of it would be Bible quotes but you know one of the pieces like “Gates of Justice” is a combination of Old Testament, New Testament, and Martin Luther King. And Dan and I both know that you know like there are so many misconceptions about my dad but one of them is that he wrote all this music that had Biblical text and you might conclude oh he’s Jimmy Swaggart that plays jazz piano or something. But as far as he’s concerned the Biblical text is just a way to nail everyone for their fake Christian attitudes and the hypocrisy. You know I’m going to point out to you in the Bible where Jesus is pointing out exactly what you’re doing that’s racist. Or after Kent State, you know I was the age, I was in high school and we did a piece he wrote called “Truth is Fallen.” It was like from Isaiah. “Truth is fallen in the streets and equity cannot enter.” Like a national guard shot college kids who were just, you know, having a good time and trying to put flowers in their guns. And what the hell is happening in America? But the most powerful way to say that instead of him saying it is quote the Bible and ram it right up there you know. You pretend you’re Christians, you know, how would Jesus have handled the situation?
